chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, raising it (to the Prophet), said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a speech of his: 'There will be a year after me in which the Believer eats in one gut, and the Infidel eats in seven guts.'

key_terms.سَنَةٌ: A year or a period of time

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the eating habits of believers versus disbelievers during times of scarcity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi’s chapter on abhorrence of abundant eating uses the metaphor of 'one stomach' versus 'seven stomachs' to contrast the spiritual and physical modesty of the believer with the insatiable greed of the disbeliever. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as literal gluttony but as a sign of spiritual poverty and lack of contentment (qana'ah) in the latter, who consume resources without gratitude or restraint. The narration serves as a practical warning against excess in consumption as a marker of faith versus disbelief.
